article.title: Homebuyers are canceling sales at near-record rates
article.summary:
Homebuyers are backing out of contracts at near-record rates, a potential sign of how higher mortgage rates are prompting buyers to rethink their plans.

Indeed, metro areas that are notably buyer's markets, like Jacksonville and Tampa, Fla., and Las Vegas, all had contract cancellation rates approaching 20%, higher than anywhere else in the country.

Outside the cafe in the park, when the gas has cleared, 27-year-old activist Sidorela Vatnikaj, a masters student, describes her typical day.
She is uncomfortable with the violence towards the authorities from her fellow protesters, but blames the police for starting and fuelling it.
"They come from families whose family members had no other choice than to leave the country - a million in the past decade.
"We need a technocratic government for one year, to prepare the country for real, democratic elections," Vatnikaj replies.
Young people in Albania feel encouraged by their fellow Gen Z protesters around the world, Vatnikaj said.

article.title: Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month
article.summary:
"We would have it to ‌talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization," Trump told reporters outside the White House.
Trump has also sought stable relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who in turn has nurtured close ties with Putin.
Speaking about the possible meeting on Monday, Trump said, "I would do it, not so much for Ukraine because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine."
China, Russia and the United States are all members of APEC.
On Monday, Trump downplayed ​the idea of another high-profile meeting in China, with North Korean ‌leader Kim Jong Un.

Earlier this month, when asked twice by TIME magazine if Netanyahu should be given another term, Trump pivoted to his own popularity in Israel and Washington’s actions supporting Israel.
When asked whether he trusted Netanyahu, Trump replied, “I don’t trust anybody, honestly”.
But like Vakil, he cautioned against treating Trump’s endorsement as a game-changer.
Krieg said Trump was prioritising the use of “coercive leverage” through his endorsement of Netanyahu but not necessarily “war over diplomacy”.

article.title: Istanbul to host global mediation conference
article.summary:
Istanbul to host global mediation conferenceISTANBULTurkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan (AA Photo)Türkiye will host the ninth Istanbul Mediation Conference on Oct. 23-24 under the theme “Partnerships and New Perspectives for Peace: Mediation in a Changing World,” the Turkish Foreign Ministry said on Oct. 19.
The conference will be held under the auspices of Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan amid rapid and profound changes in global dynamics, the ministry said in a statement.
Türkiye, which has played an active role in promoting the peaceful resolution of conflicts, launched the “Mediation for Peace” initiative at the U.N. in 2010.
Türkiye has hosted the Istanbul Mediation Conferences since 2012, establishing the event as a leading international platform for conflict resolution, preventive diplomacy and mediation.
The ninth edition is expected to bring together relevant stakeholders to promote dialogue and address current challenges in mediation.

article.title: Israel’s ties with Europe are fraying. Can its election change that?
article.summary:
European condemnation of Netanyahu is mounting, but analysts say Israel’s election offers little prospect of a material change for Palestinians.
Share Israel’s ties with Europe are fraying.
“Europe and Israel are bound to be friends and allies,” the European Commission president said on April 23, 2023.
Israel played international football in Europe, competed in Eurovision and shared intelligence with European governments.
Those ties still exist, but have since become battlegrounds after Israel’s systematic destruction of Gaza, which has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians.
